$comment: Machine-readable inventory of business data access that still bypasses /api/v1, per the brief's requirement to leave one when full conversion exceeds a single run. Counts are from architecture/inventory/{web,mobile}-supabase-usage.json, generated 2026-07-26. 'owner' is the module that will own the operation once migrated, matching the module boundaries in the brief.

totals.note: No business write has been migrated yet. Phases 2, 3 and 6 delivered the foundation (migrations, layering+enforcement, entitlement engine); the vertical slices are next and are ordered below.

priorities.why: The load status state machine runs in a React component. The status update and its audit-event insert are two separate non-transactional writes, so a failure between them yields a status change with no audit record. The same file already calls PATCH /api/loads/:id at line 179, so two write paths for one aggregate coexist.

Replays supabase.from(entry.table as any).update(patch) — arbitrary table/patch pairs persisted in AsyncStorage. This is a generic table-write primitive on the client and cannot be preserved under a REST API; it must be redesigned to queue API commands carrying an Idempotency-Key.
priorities.targetEndpoint: n/a — client redesign; queue commands, not table patches

priorities.why: 19 writes issued straight from client components across 13 tables (documents, maintenance logs, fuel stops, IFTA crossings, driver pay config). RLS is the only authorization control and there is no server-side validation in front of any of them.

Upload-then-insert and delete-row-then-remove-blob, with inconsistent ordering between the four web components. Partial failure orphans either a row or a blob. Mobile deletes blobs directly from the client.
Delete-then-insert replace on tax-filing data with no transaction. A failure between the two loses the quarter's crossings for that load.
Resolves the target org from an inbound email 'to:' header — attacker-controlled — then writes a load with the service-role client. Widest blast radius of the unauthenticated entry points.
Pulls the entire auth user table (perPage 1000) on a per-tenant page and filters in memory. Role-gated, but the data crosses every tenant boundary before the filter runs.

Any authenticated user may pass an arbitrary load id and learn about another carrier's IFTA state. Not fixed in 0003 because adding a carrier_org_id predicate changes results for existing callers; the call sites must move behind a service first.
priorities.targetEndpoint: n/a — fix in migration once callers are migrated

priorities.why: All 21 gates still call the legacy has_feature()/get_my_entitlements() RPCs, which ignore billing_status, trial_ends_at, grace_period_until, org_flag_overrides and platform_flags. EntitlementService.hasFeatureCompat() exists so these migrate one at a time. NOTE: migrating a call site may start denying access it previously allowed (expired trial / canceled org) — that is the defect being fixed and is why each move is reviewed individually.

The only Realtime usage carrying business meaning: live driver-chat delivery. Updates and deletes never propagate, and the read-receipt update at line 92 is fired without await or error handling. Realtime must become a nonauthoritative 're-fetch' nudge. Mobile's equivalent subscription (driver-chat-section.tsx:67) is already pure UX refresh and needs no change.

20 service-role call sites; lib/api-auth.ts re-exports createAdminClient, widening the privileged import surface beyond lib/supabase/server for no benefit. Each site needs review against 'isolate, minimize, audit'.
priorities.targetEndpoint: n/a — narrow imports, add audit wrapper
